articles.headline: Raiders name Fernando Mendoza starting QB after trading Kirk Cousins
articles.description: No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza was officially named the Raiders' starting quarterback Tuesday after the team traded Kirk Cousins to the Vikings.
articles.headlineJa: レイダース、カーク・カズンズの放出後にフェルナンド・メンドーサを先発QBに指名
articles.descriptionJa: レイダースはカーク・カズンズをバイキングスへトレードした後、火曜日にドラフト1位指名のフェルナンド・メンドーサを正式に先発クォーターバックに指名した。
articles.body:
HENDERSON, Nev. -- The Fernando Mendoza era has begun in Las Vegas.

The 2026 No. 1 pick has been named the Raiders' starting quarterback after veteran Kirk Cousins was traded to the Minnesota Vikings on Tuesday, general manager John Spytek announced.

Mendoza's first career start will be Sunday at home against the reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks. This will be Mendoza's second appearance this season. He made his NFL debut late in a Week 5 loss to the New England Patriots, completing 6 of 8 passes for 48 yards.

Spytek said Mendoza "passed every test." 

"It's something that he's worked very hard for since the moment he walked into this building," Spytek said of Mendoza. "I want to stop short of saying he's earned it, but he put us in a position where we had to make a really hard decision today, with his growth as a person, as a teammate, as a leader, as a quarterback."

Spytek said the move does not mean the Raiders, who at 4-5 are still in the playoff hunt, are punting on the season and looking ahead to 2027.

"That is not the intention of this," Spytek said. "We have a big game this week against the defending world champs, and we intend to attack it like we would any week. That's expected of us."

Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Mendoza "exceeded" the team's expectations during practice. While Mendoza waited his turn, he still carried himself as though he was the starter. He wore his helmet through the game and stood close to quarterbacks coach Mike Sullivan, reciting playcalls that he heard through the headset device in his helmet.

Mendoza also spent late nights on the team's indoor practice field, going over the game plan.

Over time, Kubiak noticed Mendoza make improvements in his accuracy, command of the offense, his ability to get in and out of a huddle and his operation of two-minute drills.

Kubiak added that Mendoza proved he's ready not just physically but mentally. Mendoza was in the building Tuesday studying for the team's upcoming game.

"He puts a lot of work in," Kubiak said. "His teammates know how prepared he is. It's not just lip service, but he has shown it on the practice field."

Kubiak said he knew this day was coming but didn't know exactly when.

The Raiders selected Mendoza in hopes of him becoming their franchise quarterback, adding stability at the position for the foreseeable future. He showcased the potential to fill that role during his lone season at Indiana. The Heisman Trophy winner threw for career highs in passing yards (3,535), touchdown passes (41), completion rate (72%) and QBR (90.3) while helping the Hoosiers win their first national title.

Las Vegas believed Mendoza's accuracy, athleticism and strong IQ fit Kubiak's offensive scheme. At the same time, the Raiders wanted to be patient with Mendoza's development. Spytek said they had discussions with Mendoza during his predraft interview about the plans they had for him.

articles.headline: What the Kirk Cousins trade means for the Vikings and the Raiders
articles.description: We answered big questions surrounding the trade of quarterback Kirk Cousins from the Raiders to the Vikings.
articles.headlineJa: カーク・カズンズのトレードがバイキングスとレイダースにもたらす影響
articles.descriptionJa: レイダースからバイキングスへのクォーターバック、カーク・カズンズのトレードを巡る重要な疑問に答える。
articles.body:
Kirk Cousins played what appeared to be his final game for the Minnesota Vikings on Oct. 29, 2023. 

On that afternoon at Lambeau Field, Cousins had thrown for 274 yards and two touchdowns when he tore his right Achilles tendon and was lost for the season. That moment set off a three-year odyssey that improbably ended the way it began. 

Cousins returned Tuesday to the Vikings, via a trade that sent their 2027 third-round draft pick to the Las Vegas Raiders, and could start Sunday's game against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field (1 p.m. ET, Fox). Since then, the Vikings have tried eight different starting quarterbacks and made a total of 14 different in-season quarterback changes. 

The most recent came Monday night at U.S. Bank Stadium, where Carson Wentz -- starting in place of the injured Kyler Murray -- produced the Vikings' worst game by a starting quarterback since 2006. The Vikings have lost consecutive games after a 6-0 start, and their decision-makers did not want to waste what has been an elite-level defense and special teams performance this season with poor quarterback play. 

In Las Vegas, the door is now wide open for Fernando Mendoza, the No. 1 pick of the 2026 NFL draft, to step into his role as the long-term franchise quarterback.

ESPN Vikings reporter Kevin Seifert, Raiders reporter Ryan McFadden, national reporter Jeremy Fowler and fantasy's Michael F. Florio take a closer look at the questions and issues involved.

What's a realistic expectation for the Vikings' offense with Cousins at QB?

The offense under coach Kevin O'Connell has been tough for quarterbacks of all experience levels to master, and Cousins talked often in 2022 about his struggles to feel comfortable in it. But by the middle of the 2023 season, Cousins was playing better than he ever had in a Minnesota uniform. He led the NFL with 18 touchdown passes over eight games and had a 64 QBR. All of which goes to say that if he can pick up where he left off, the Vikings could soon resurrect their dormant passing offense. But it's only natural to expect Cousins to need some time to adjust after three years away, and it also might be a generous assumption that the quarterback position is the only cause of their issues this season. It's only fair to say that playcalling, pass protection and run game efficiency have also contributed. -- Seifert

If Cousins isn't able to ignite the Vikings' offense, what does it mean for Kevin O'Connell's future in Minnesota?

If that is the outcome, and the Vikings miss the playoffs following a 6-0 start, there won't be many people left to blame. Owners Zygi and Mark Wilf have already fired general manager Kwesi Adofo-Mensah, whom they hired alongside O'Connell in 2022. O'Connell reports directly to the Wilfs, not to new general manager Nolan Teasley, but the Vikings' offensive collapse now goes all the way back to the start of the 2025 season. articles.headline: From 2-7 to 6-2: Josh Downs reacts to Chiefs trade with Vince Carter GIF
articles.description: A moment from Vince Carter's retirement ceremony helped Downs sum up his feelings about joining Kansas City.
articles.body:
Josh Downs needed only one GIF to show how he felt about going from the 2-7 Indianapolis Colts to the 6-2 Kansas City Chiefs.

After Tuesday's trade, the wide receiver posted a popular clip of Vince Carter overcome with emotion during his Toronto Raptors jersey retirement ceremony. Often used to celebrate good news, the GIF presumably represented Downs' feelings about his new destination.

The moment dates to Nov. 2, 2024, when Carter became the first player to have his jersey retired by the Raptors. His emotional reaction as Toronto honored his No. 15 has since taken on a life of its own online.

Downs' post also caught the attention of his new quarterback, Patrick Mahomes, who reposted it with a clock emoji.

Downs, who had requested a trade, heads to Kansas City with a 2027 seventh-round pick in exchange for fourth- and fifth-round selections. He brings 33 catches for 354 yards and a touchdown this season to a Chiefs receiver group dealing with injuries to Tyquan Thornton and Xavier Worthy.

The GIF wasn't Downs' only message Tuesday. He also thanked the team that drafted him in the third round in 2023.

"I am beyond grateful and blessed for my time in Indy. Nothing but love For the Shoe," he wrote on X.

articles.headline: Fantasy football consistency ratings: 2024 to 2026
articles.description: The consistency ratings weigh both how consistent and how start-worthy players have been from 2024 to 2026.
articles.body:
Updated Nov. 10, 2026 (through Week 9 of 2026)

How consistency ratings work

Using fantasy points determined by ESPN's standard scoring, the charts contained in this column rate players based upon how consistently reliable they have been during the 2024 through 2026 seasons, a span of 45 weeks' worth of games (18 weeks apiece in 2024 and 2025, nine so far in 2026). For IDPs (individual defensive players), the scoring from our weekly rankings is used: solo tackle (1.5), assisted tackle (0.75), tackle for loss (2), sack (4), interception (5), forced fumble (4), fumble recovery (4), touchdown (6), safety (2), pass defended (1.5). To familiarize you with the terminology and column headers listed in the charts below:

Start%: The player's "start percentage," which shows how often he earned a start in an ESPN standard PPR (points per reception) league. This is his number of "starts" -- those defined below -- divided by his number of scheduled team games.

CR: The player's "consistency rating," which is calculated as his weekly standard deviation divided by his PPR fantasy points per game average. This is meant to identify the players who were most consistently close to their weekly averages. The lower the number, the more consistent the player. Again, lower numbers are better.

nPPR%: The player's start percentage using non-PPR scoring, using ESPN's standard scoring settings without any points per reception.

FPTS/G: The player's average PPR fantasy points scored per game.

Start: The number of times that the player's point total in a given week was worthy of having had him active in an ESPN standard PPR league.

Star: The number of times the player's point total ranked among the best at his position.

Stiff: The number of times the player's point total ranked among the worst at his position, making almost any waiver-wire option a smarter choice.

These are the benchmarks for what constitutes a "start," "star" or "stiff" performance:

Sat: The number of times the player sat out a game. Players are not charged "stiff" points for sitting out, nor does it impact their overall consistency rating (CR), but it hurts their overall start percentage.

Players must have a start rate of at least 20% in either standard PPR or non-PPR scoring, rank among the top 20 quarterbacks, tight ends or kickers, top 50 running backs or wide receivers, or top 40 defensive linemen, linebackers or defensive backs, in terms of total fantasy points at their position from 2024 to 2026, or are averaging at least 50 snaps per game, for inclusion in the chart. All defense/special teams are included regardless of whether they meet those minimums.

articles.headline: Warriors lose guard Brandon Williams to mild hamstring strain
articles.description: The Warriors will be without reserve guard Brandon Williams for at least a week after he strained his left hamstring during Monday night's win, sources told ESPN.
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors will be without reserve guard Brandon Williams for at least a week after he strained his left hamstring during Monday night's 138-87 win over the New Orleans Pelicans, the team announced Tuesday. 

Williams entered late in the first quarter, burst to the rim for two quick layups but came up hobbled on the second and limped to the locker room after only 99 seconds of action.

The Warriors soon announced that Williams was out with a hamstring issue and scheduled for an MRI. Those results revealed the mild strain, ruling him out for the Warriors' difficult upcoming road trip to Houston, San Antonio, New Orleans, Dallas and Memphis.

 

Williams has been an immediate bench spark in his first season with the Warriors, averaging 10.4 points and 2.3 assists in only 16.4 minutes per game, providing scoring punch the moment Stephen Curry rests. Williams has 17 and 20 points in the two games that Curry missed this season, including a win over the LA Clippers as part of the Warriors' current eight-game win streak.

But left hamstring issues have followed Williams early in his NBA career. He strained it in the 2025 preseason while with Dallas and subsequently missed time last March while dealing with tightness.

The Warriors, while surging at 8-3, are significantly depleted. Starting wings Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody are rehabbing serious knee injuries, projected starting center Kristaps Porzingis has stepped away from basketball entirely and they lost backup guard Will Richard to a UCL tear in his left thumb over the weekend.

Richard has been upgraded to questionable for the Warriors' game in Houston on Wednesday night. He has explored the feasibility of wearing a splint on his left thumb and playing through the injury. Gary Payton II is out with left knee inflammation.

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Barcelona eye move for Bayern's Tah
articles.description: Barcelona are looking to improve their defense and could look to Bayern Munich's Jonathan Tah as an option. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
Barcelona have made an enquiry about signing Bayern Munich center back Jonathan Tah, while the Arsenal trio of Martín Zubimendi, Viktor Gyökeres and Mikel Merino could depart to raise funds for more arrivals. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Barcelona have made an enquiry about signing Bayern Munich center back Jonathan Tah, as reported by Sky Sports Deutschland. The Blaugrana are focusing on the 30-year-old ahead of January, with the club's sporting director Deco looking for an experienced defender who can play alongside youngster Pau Cubarsí and bring stability and leadership qualities. Bayern have little interest in letting Tah leave, especially as he is a key part of their plans and has a contract that runs until 2029, while the Germany international is also not considering a transfer.

- Atlético Madrid are one of the main clubs showing an interest in Arsenal midfielder Martín Zubimendi, as confirmed by Diario Sport. There is a good relationship between the two clubs and Los Colchoneros' interest in the 27-year-old stretches back to his time with Real Sociedad, while the Gunners need to offload players to help balance their books. Viktor Gyökeres and Mikel Merino could also leave the Emirates to help Arsenal's finances, according to AS. The trio have all struggled for playing time this season.

- Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur are interested in Real Sociedad striker Orri Óskarsson, according to Calciomercato. The 22-year-old has caught the eye with his performances this season, already having 14 goals and six assists to his name across LaLiga and the Europa League. The Red Devils are interested due to Benjamin Sesko's injury absence, while Spurs are looking for a striker to suit Roberto De Zerbi's style of play. Everton, Brentford and Sunderland are also interested in Óskarsson, while Atalanta have previously been linked, though any offer to sign the Iceland international would need to exceed €20 million.

- Liverpool and Real Madrid are on a growing list of clubs monitoring Brighton & Hove Albion goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen, according to TEAMtalk. The Reds are looking at the 24-year-old as they plan for whenever veteran stopper Alisson Becker departs Anfield, while Los Blancos see the Netherlands international as a possible successor to Thibaut Courtois. Chelsea and Manchester United are also long-term admirers, while Bayern are also tracking his progress having previously made enquiries.

- Juventus are looking at Atlético's Alexander Sørloth, Monaco's Folarin Balogun and Al Qadsiah's Mateo Retegui as they aim to sign a striker in the January transfer window, according to Gazzetta dello Sport. Sørloth in particular is a favorite for Juve, who have held a long-term interest in the 30-year-old. articles.headline: MrBeast, meet Haaland: Man City star puts YouTuber through soccer gauntlet
articles.description: Manchester City star Erling Haaland has collaborated with popular YouTuber "MrBeast" in a series of various soccer challenges.
articles.headlineJa: MrBeastがハーランドと対面：マン・シティのスターがYouTuberにサッカーの試練を与える
articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・シティのスター、アーリング・ハーランドが、人気YouTuberの「MrBeast」とコラボレーションし、一連の様々なサッカーチャレンジを行った。
articles.body:
Manchester City star Erling Haaland is known for his extraordinary feats on a soccer pitch, but this time he decided to put that to the test by allowing famous YouTube star James Stephen "Jimmy" Donaldson -- better known as "MrBeast"  -- to participate in a series of intense soccer challenges known as the "Erling Haaland Gauntlet" at the club's training ground.

Posted on the Norway international's YouTube channel, which currently has over four million subscribers, Haaland put MrBeast -- alongside his two friends Tareq Salameh and Nolan Hansen -- through several soccer challenges to test their skill, strength and endurance. 

The challenges consisted of sprints, wall sits, headers and a crossbar challenge, in which the winner would get a "Haaland Hammer," and the loser would have to go into goal and get hit by free shots from the penalty spot.

In the end, it was Salameh who ended up winning the "Haaland Hammer" after finishing first amongst the three, and it was MrBeast who had the misfortune of getting hit with shots from his two friends and, of course, Haaland.

It's safe to say that the most-subscribed YouTuber with over 526 million -- who's known for his extraordinary challenges -- probably doesn't have what it takes to cut it as a professional soccer player. 

While it is currently the international break, that doesn't mean Haaland will relax while there are no matches for Manchester City. The 26-year-old was called up to play for his national team this month against Wales and Denmark in the final matches of their UEFA Nations League A campaign.

They are currently last in Group 4, as they look to qualify for the quarterfinal of the competition.

articles.headline: Karabell's notebook: Harden's declining role, Garland's TOs, a rookie to watch
articles.description: Eric Karabell empties out the notebook with all that he's noticing around the NBA and what it means for fantasy.
articles.headlineJa: カラベルのノート：ハーデンの役割の縮小、ガーランドのターンオーバー、注目すべきルーキー
articles.descriptionJa: エリック・カラベルが、NBA界隈で注目している事項と、それがファンタジー・スポーツにどのような影響を与えるかをまとめる。
articles.body:
It's easy to claim otherwise today, but there was little indication Cleveland Cavaliers PG/SG James Harden would suddenly become a fantasy disappointment this season. After all, Harden was terrific last season, averaging 43.5 ESPN fantasy points per game. Only 16 players scored more. Harden was 36 years old.

Is there really much difference between being 36 and 37 years old? (Guess I will find out in a few years when I turn 37, lol.) Harden may not have deserved a second-round slot in ESPN average live drafts, but there was regression built into projections and he fell to Round 4.

Harden is 11 games into the season and he's not performing as a top-50 fantasy option, certainly not yet anyway at 29.1 fantasy points per game, and many are whispering that this is the end of his time as a top point guard. It is fine if Immanuel Quickley, Fred VanVleet or Coby White average 15.3 PPG, 4.8 RPG and only 5.7 APG, but certainly not if Harden does so.

Perhaps we didn't expect quite another 20.5 PPG, 4.8 RPG and 7.7 APG (his numbers in 26 games with the Cavaliers after the LA Clippers trade), but the current numbers are just not cool.

Is it reasonable to ask if this is all we're going to get this season? Perhaps it is, but there is a bigger picture going on with Cleveland. Harden has only 13 assists and nine turnovers in his past three outings, only one of them a win (over the Philadelphia 76ers, of course).

He won't shoot a ghastly 36.4% from the field for long, but watching Harden and his missing usage it is clear he is more willing to defer shots and in directing the offense. His field goal attempts are down from 16 per game to 12, and free throw attempts down from 7.5 per game to 4.8. His minutes are also down. Hmm.

Typically, this would be a wise time to trade for Harden, so I will gently side with that one, with some caveat: It would be quite surprising if Harden finishes among the top 20 fantasy scorers again. Then again, the Cavaliers may be pacing all their stars for better playoff performance.

Who is earning Cleveland's shots? SG/PG Donovan Mitchell has seen his usage crumble as well, scoring 22.8 PPG, when last season it was 27.9 PPG. Even PF/C Evan Mobley is underachieving across the board, as he falls even further from potential 20-PPG, 10-RPG production.

Perhaps the Cavaliers are handling things perfectly here. The bench is certainly improved, with impressive second-round rookie SG Meleek Thomas hitting 47.8% of his 3-pointers and Croatian journeyman SF Mario Hezonja, back in the NBA after six seasons overseas, contributing a useful 19.9 MPG. Newcomer SF/PF Peyton Watson, who was more valuable in fantasy as a Denver Nugget last season, has solidified a starting role.

Yes, Harden (and to a lesser extent Mitchell and Mobley) are disappointing fantasy managers, but that appears to be, in a roundabout way, Cleveland's actual plan.

articles.description: UE Cornellà gained global fame when Lionel Messi purchased them earlier this year. Why has the GOAT bought a semi-professional club in Spain's fifth tier?
articles.body:
BARCELONA -- Last month, a club owned by Lionel Messi beat Manchester City, Inter Milan and Arsenal to reach the final of a prestigious cup competition. This did not happen in a game of Football Manager, or EA FC. It actually happened. UE Cornellà, the tiny team from Spain's fifth tier, went up against the best in the world and beat them.

The twist is that it was not the first team. At the same time as Cornellà's under-16 side were beating Arsenal in Miami in the Messi Cup, the senior side were having a much less glamorous afternoon back in a drizzly Barcelona.

A second-half strike from Marc Esteban earned a point for Ignasi Senabre's side against FE Grama in Spanish soccer's semi-professional fifth tier. But it did little to improve on what has been a disappointing season so far for the club taken over in April by former Argentina and Barcelona star Messi.

- Messi bought a club! What you need to know about UE Cornellà

- Watch replays of all 2026 Messi Cup matches on ESPN+ (U.S.)

- Messi tracker: All of his goals, assists and key moments in 2026

Messi's takeover prompted talk, admittedly outside of Cornellà circles, of 'doing a Wrexham.' The term is a nod to the Welsh side's rapid rise through the English football pyramid, from non-league to within one promotion of the Premier League, under Hollywood stars Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac.

"The comparison is understandable because in both cases there is a world-famous figure involved," a source at the Catalan club tells ESPN. "But they are very different projects, contexts and models. Each club has its own project."

So what does Messi want Cornellà to become? Is the ambition to take the first team up to LaLiga, or does he see greater potential in the academy and the community?

Messi's Cornellà takeover shocked everyone

Cornellà coach Senabre initially thought the announcement regarding Messi was a hoax.

"I found out via the press," Senabre tells ESPN. "All of a sudden everyone was talking about it, but before then it hadn't come out anywhere. I thought it was AI at first."

Next thing Senabre knew, he was ushered into a meeting room at the club's modest stadium, which doubles as their training ground. The Camp Municipal de Cornellà sits literally in the shadows of neighbouring LaLiga club Espanyol's RCDE Stadium. The two grounds are separated by a 10-metre-wide walkway in Cornellà de Llobregat on the southern outskirts of Barcelona, where Messi spent 20 years of his life.

There, alongside his staff and the players, he watched a five-minute introduction video sent by Messi. The introduction, of course, was hardly necessary. Everyone knew who Messi was, but a source says it's an example of how involved he has been from the start.

articles.headline: Xavi Simons reveals emotional toll of Spurs ACL injury as return nears
articles.description: Injured Tottenham attacker Xavi Simons has spoken of the anguish he felt watching the club's relegation battle last season, but is working "endless hours" to return for Roberto De Zerbi's side.
articles.headlineJa: シャビ・シモンズ、復帰が近づく中、スパーズでのACL負傷による精神的苦痛を明かす
articles.descriptionJa: 怪我に泣いたトッテナムのアタッカー、シャビ・シモンズは、昨シーズンのチームの降格争いを目の当たりにした苦悩について語ったが、ロベルト・デ・ゼルビ率いるチームへの復帰に向けて「果てしない時間」をトレーニングに費やしている。
articles.body:
Injured Tottenham attacker Xavi Simons has spoken of the anguish he felt watching the club's relegation battle last season, but is working "endless hours" to return for Roberto De Zerbi's side.

Xavi sustained anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) damage during a 1-0 win at Wolves on April 25 which ruled the Netherlands playmaker out of Spurs' final four fixtures along with the World Cup last summer.

However, Xavi, 23, has been ahead of schedule through his rehabilitation and is set to enter phase three of his recovery later in November, which will allow him to resume team training.

Last month, the former Barcelona and Paris St Germain youngster was invited to speak at the Oxford Union and went into detail about his current spell on the sidelines.

Speaking on Oct. 30, Xavi told students: "I had to watch the remainder of the season from my hospital bed and let me tell you it was not easy.

"I felt completely out of control, infuriated because I couldn't contribute and help. I couldn't do a thing. Luckily the boys did their job.

"Mental is just as important as physical. I've had bad moments at night, not even my family know how bad. I've cried, I've wanted so bad to contribute to Spurs, to my national team.

"I read books, I enhanced my knowledge on certain things, I wanted more information, I wanted to stimulate my mind. I wanted calmness in my brain. That was as important as going to the gym every day.

- Tottenham's winning run brought to abrupt end by late Noah Okafor winner

- Leeds condemn 'disgusting' alleged racist abuse of Jayden Bogle after Spurs game

"It's ultimately finding the balance. You can't underestimate the importance of good psychological health. If your brain isn't working, your body isn't working."

ACL ruptures generally have a recovery time of around nine months, but Xavi is in line to feature in first-team training again after the international break.

That would put him back in contact training only seven months after suffering the injury and raises the possibility of a return to competitive action before the nine-month mark at the end of January.

Quizzed during a question-and-answer session about how he plans to return at his best, Xavi said: "My knee has to feel good. I need to feel strong. Right now, I'm on track, I'm getting stronger every day.

"I'm putting in endless hours. I have a great team that has been with me this entire journey. Everyone has a different schedule.

"Everyone's journey is different. For me, I want to come home and only think, 'I can't move my legs anymore,' because I have pushed myself to the limit daily.

"I want to feel tired. That feeling is when I allow myself to rest. That's how I've approached it throughout."

articles.headline: Vincent Kompany returns to Bayern Munich training for first time since collapse
articles.description: Bayern Munich manager Vincent Kompany has made a return to the club's base for the first time since he collapsed in a training session.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich manager Vincent Kompany has made a return to the club's base for the first time since he collapsed in a training session.

The 40-year-old was taken ill during a second-team training session on Oct. 23 and was diagnosed with meningeal irritation which has forced him to miss Bayern's last five matches.

The club also confirmed that Kompany is now "on the road to recovery" and will complete rehabilitation on an injured shoulder at the their Sabener Strasse training ground.

Kompany was pictured at the training base with his arm in a sling after he reportedly dislocated his shoulder when he collapsed.

In Kompany's absence, assistant coach Aaron Danks took charge of the team and oversaw a 2-0 Champions League victory over Atlético Madrid as well as a 2-2 draw in the top-of-the-table clash with Borussia Dortmund.

- Bayern Munich's Manuel Neuer set for spell on sidelines with foot injury

- Transfer rumors, news: Liverpool's Rio Ngumoha still a Bayern Munich target

Bayern sporting director Max Eberl has been providing regular updates on Kompany's recovery but it remains to be seen when he will make a return to the touchline. Bayern's first match after the international break is against Cologne at the Allianz Arena on Friday Nov. 20.

Bayern are top of the Bundesliga on goal difference from Borussia Dortmund.

articles.headline: Virgil van Dijk: 'No panic' over uncertain Liverpool future
articles.description: Virgil van Dijk has said he is "not in any panic" about his Liverpool future despite the fact his contract is set to expire next summer.
articles.body:
Virgil van Dijk has said he is "not in any panic" about his Liverpool future despite the fact his contract is set to expire next summer.

The 35-year-old penned a two-year extension at Anfield in April 2024 and remains an ever-present in the Reds' back line. He has played every minute for Liverpool in the Premier League this season but says he is not concerned about the prospect of his current deal running out.

"I feel good but it's not about me at the moment," Van Dijk said. "Let's see. I'm not in any panic."

"I want to keep playing and continue what I'm doing. Let's see what the season brings. I've had an amazing time already so far. If that will be extended, that's the case.

- Alisson in talks over new Liverpool contract: 'I'm happy to stay'

- Liverpool's Barcola, Isak, Wirtz show signs they're finally starting to click

- If Arsenal find attacking spark, they could run away with the Premier League

"If not, then I will go somewhere else. There's nothing to report at the moment but that doesn't mean that there's any stress or anything." 

Van Dijk has withdrawn from international duty ahead of the Netherlands' Nations League matches with Greece and Germany, having been carrying a knock during his recent outings for Liverpool.

Reflecting on the club's progress under new head coach Andoni Iraola, the defender said: "It's a work in progress. Some games we could have done much better ... And some games we lost but we were good. We're trying to find consistency as that's the only way to be successful."
